consent.title: Before we begin — a few things you should know.
consent.body: The questions that follow are about your health and how you are feeling. We use your answers only to give you a personalised roadmap — articles, resources, and a doctor-ready summary tailored to you.
consent.body2: We do not sell your information. We do not share it with anyone without your permission. You can delete your data at any time. This platform is compliant with the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA).
consent.control: You are in control of your information. Always.
consent.checkbox: I understand and I agree to continue.

q3.hint: Used with your height to calculate BMI for your doctor download.

q4.text: When did your periods last change or stop?

q5.text: Has a doctor ever spoken to you about menopause or hormones?

q7.text: Memory problems — forgetting names, words, or where you put things

q8.text: Word-finding difficulty — knowing what you want to say but not being able to find the word

q9.text: Reduced ability to multitask — struggling to manage more than one thing at a time

q10.text: Mood swings — feeling up and down for no clear reason

q11.text: Irritability — snapping or getting frustrated more easily than usual

q12.text: Feeling anxious or worried more than usual

q14.text: Low motivation — struggling to find the energy or desire to do things you used to enjoy

q15.text: Low self-worth — feeling less confident or less valuable than before

q16.text: Not feeling like yourself — not recognising the person you have become
q16.hint: This question catches many women for the first time. Trust what you feel.

q17.hint: You can answer honestly. If you're struggling, Mandi will put support on your roadmap right away.

q18.text: Hot flushes — sudden waves of heat through your body

q19.text: Night sweats — waking drenched or overheated

q20.text: Sleep problems — difficulty falling or staying asleep

q21.text: Heart palpitations — your heart racing or beating irregularly

q22.text: Headaches or migraines — more frequent or more severe than before

q24.text: Restless legs — an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially at night

q25.text: Tinnitus — ringing or buzzing in the ears

q26.text: Joint pain — aching, stiffness, or swelling in joints

q27.text: Muscle pain — generalised aching in muscles

q28.text: Frozen shoulder — pain or restricted movement in the shoulder
q28.hint: An under-recognised menopause symptom. If this is you, you are not imagining it.

q29.text: Fatigue and low energy — exhausted even after rest

q30.text: Weight gain — especially around the middle

q32.text: Skin changes — dryness, itchiness, or texture changes

q34.text: Dry eyes — persistent dryness, irritation, or blurry vision

q35.text: Changes in your period — heavier, lighter, longer, shorter, or more irregular than before

q38.text: Bladder issues — urgency, leaking, or needing to go more often, including at night

q41.text: Reduced alcohol tolerance — two glasses that used to be fine now feel like four
q41.hint: This is the question that makes women say: 'wait — that is menopause?'

q42.text: New or worsening allergies — hay fever, food intolerances, or sensitivities you never had before

q43.text: Worsening of a long-term health condition — asthma, migraine, autoimmune condition, or similar
q43.hint: If this is a strong yes, Mandi will route you to specialist-led care.

q44.text: Impact on your ability to work — concentration, productivity, or confidence at work

q45.text: Impact on your relationship with your partner

q46.text: Impact on your relationships with family — children, parents, close relatives

q47.text: Impact on your social life — withdrawing, not wanting to go out

q48.text: Impact on your ability to stay active and exercise

q49.text: When you think about what you have been experiencing — what is your gut feeling?
q49.a: Something is wrong and I need help now.
q49.b: It is probably just ageing — I will manage.
q49.c: I have tried everything. Nothing works for me.
q49.d: I have done my research — I know what is happening.

q50.text: How do you feel about hormone therapy (HRT)?
q50.a: Open to it if a doctor recommends it.
q50.b: I prefer natural approaches — herbs, lifestyle, supplements.
q50.c: I am nervous — I have heard it can be risky.
q50.d: I am already on HRT, or I have already tried it.

q51.text: How do you feel about the medical system when it comes to your health?
q51.a: I trust my doctor — I just need the right referral.
q51.b: My symptoms have been dismissed. I feel unseen.
q51.c: I prefer to research first before going to a doctor.
q51.d: I honestly do not know where to start.

q52.text: Have you ever felt embarrassed or ashamed about what you have been experiencing?
q52.d: I had not thought about it.

q53.text: Do you ever feel like it might be too late to get help — that you missed the window?

q54.text: Do you have any existing health conditions that make you worry about hormone treatment?
q54.hint: Choose all that apply. Your answer helps Mandi route you to the right care.
q54.notSure: Not sure — I would like guidance

q55.text: What would feel most useful to you today?
q55.a: Understand what is happening in my body.
q55.b: Know if what I am feeling is normal.
q55.c: Learn my options — HRT and alternatives.
q55.d: Find a doctor who speaks my language and understands hormones.
q55.e: Something to take to my existing doctor.

q56.text: How did you find Mandi today?
q56.hint: This helps us understand how women are hearing about the platform.

roadmap.title: Your Mandi Roadmap

mild.label: Early signals
mild.line: Your symptoms are present but manageable. This is a good time to get informed and take gentle steps.

moderate.label: Active hormonal change
moderate.line: Your symptoms are affecting your daily life. You deserve proper support — not to be told to push through.

significant.label: Significant impact
significant.line: Your symptoms are having a meaningful impact on your daily life. You deserve support now — and you can get it.

sally.headline: You have been searching. Here are your answers.
sally.body: What you are feeling is real. It has a name. And there is support available to you — starting today.

olga.headline: You may have more going on than you realised.
olga.body: Many of the things you have been putting down to stress or ageing are recognised symptoms of hormonal change.

vicky.headline: You deserve to be heard — and helped.
vicky.body: If you have been dismissed before, that was not okay. Mandi will walk with you to the right care.

nelly.headline: You know a lot. Here is what the latest evidence says.
nelly.body: Your research has served you well. Mandi will make sure your next consultation is as informed as possible.

nina.headline: Your instincts about your body are valid.
nina.body: There is a place for lifestyle and a place for medicine. Your roadmap respects both, side by side.

retha.headline: It is never too late to feel better.
retha.body: The evidence on late intervention is more positive than you may have heard. There are options worth exploring.

colleen.headline: Your situation deserves specialist input.
colleen.body: With a complex history, the right care means the right doctor — one who understands both your conditions and your hormones.

selfHarm.title: What you shared takes courage.
selfHarm.body: You are not alone in this — and you do not have to face it alone. Please reach out. The South African Depression and Anxiety Group is available 24/7.

colleen.title: Specialist-led care recommended.
colleen.body: Given your medical history, your roadmap prioritises connecting you with a specialist who can manage your hormonal health alongside your existing conditions. General HRT guidance is secondary here — your safety comes first.

book-first.title: Book a consultation
book-first.body: Based on what you shared, speaking to an HRT-informed doctor is the most important next step. Find one who speaks your language and understands hormones.

education-first.title: Understand what is happening
education-first.body: Start with the basics — what hormonal change actually looks like, and why your symptoms make sense.

normalise-first.title: You are not alone in this
normalise-first.body: Hear from other South African women who have been exactly where you are — and found their way through.

options-first.title: Know your options
options-first.body: Body-identical HRT, lifestyle approaches, integrative care — understand what is available and what the evidence says.

clinic-first.title: Find care near you
clinic-first.body: Search our directory of HRT-friendly practitioners — filtered by your language and location, including telemedicine.

download-first.title: Take it to your doctor
download-first.body: Download a one-page summary of your symptom profile, MenoScore, and questions to ask — the document that changes your consultation.

roadmap.retake: Your symptoms may change over time.

feedback.title: Does this roadmap feel right for you?
feedback.missing: Is there anything you expected to see that is missing?
feedback.thanks: Thank you — that helps us build something better for the next woman who arrives.
